official.deadline_central_display: 30 November 2026, 11:59 pm CET (applications); letters of reference by 15 December 2026
official.deadline_note: Applications run 15 October - 30 November 2026 (11:59 pm CET). All letters of recommendation must be submitted by 15 December 2026 (11:59 pm CET). Ranking by providers runs 14-25 January 2027 and internship positions are announced around February/March 2027.
official.status_note: The DAAD RISE Germany pages publish the current cycle: applications 15 October - 30 November 2026, with internship start dates between 15 May and 15 July 2027.
benefits: A monthly scholarship of 992 Euros (calculated on a daily basis for stays shorter than 23 days in a month)
Health insurance, accident and personal liability insurance
International travel subsidy and a 160 Euros travel stipend for the RISE meeting
Invitation to the RISE Germany meeting in Heidelberg in July 2027
Canadian students applying via Mitacs Globalink: 100 matched candidates receive 7,000 CAD from Mitacs towards travel and living expenses, with DAAD providing insurance
eligibility: Currently enrolled in a bachelor's degree program at a university/college in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom or Ireland in biology, chemistry, computer science, physics, earth sciences or engineering (or a closely related field)
Must have completed at least 2 years of the degree program by the time of the internship placement
Must prove that you will maintain undergraduate status after the internship - students graduating in spring or summer 2027 are not eligible and should apply to RISE Professional
International students must prove that they study at a university/college in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland for more than 12 months by the application deadline
German citizenship holders are only eligible if they can prove they have been living outside of Germany for six years or more
requirements: Apply completely online through the RISE Germany internship database - register first for a DAAD ID
Submit one motivation letter for each project applied to
Submit a CV, a list of courses (no longer than one page), a transcript and a certificate of enrollment
Have an academic referee (holding at least a PhD) upload the letter of reference online within the reference window
documents: One motivation letter per project applied to
List of courses completed by the time the internship begins (max one page)
Transcript of records (digital with university name/logo/student name and print date, or a copy of a certified hard copy)
Certificate of enrollment showing the university stamp, an authorized signature and the expected graduation date
Letter of reference on university letterhead with the referee's signature, uploaded online by the referee
selection_criteria: Internship providers submit their ranking of applicants between 14 and 25 January 2027; providers may exclude undergraduates they feel are unsuited

DAAD ranks undergraduates by academic performance (GPA) and projects by demand, then matches them in an alternating process: the top 30 projects are assigned one of their three highest-priority available applicants, then the top 30 students are assigned one of their three available projects, and so on
The motivation letter, academic performance, letter of reference, practical experience and the provider's ranking together determine the placement; no individual feedback is provided
coverage: Monthly scholarship of 992 Euros to help cover living expenses
Health insurance, accident and personal liability insurance
International travel subsidy and a 160 Euros travel stipend for the RISE meeting
Housing assistance from the host university, university of applied sciences or institute, plus matching with PhD student mentors or researchers
application_method: Register for a DAAD ID and get access to the RISE Germany internship database
Search the available internship offers without restricting the search to a single field of study
Submit the online application with the motivation letter(s), CV, list of courses, transcript and certificate of enrollment
Create the reference link in the database and send it to your professor so the letter of reference is uploaded by 15 December 2026
official.application_route: Completely online through the RISE Germany internship database; the referee uploads the letter of recommendation through a generated web link.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students enrolled at North American, British and Irish universities regardless of nationality after more than 12 months of study there; German citizens are eligible only after six years or more living outside Germany.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - non-US/Canadian/UK/Irish citizens are welcome provided they have studied at a university in those countries for more than 12 months by the application deadline; no additional documents are required.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Biology, chemistry, computer science, physics, earth sciences, engineering or a closely related field; hosts are matched to the student's area of interest.
official.duration: Three months (minimum stay ten weeks, maximum stay 90 days), with a start between 15 May and 15 July 2027.
official.description: RISE Germany offers undergraduate students from North American, British and Irish universities the opportunity to complete a summer research internship at top German universities and research institutions, and is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. Students are matched with a host according to their area of interest, German language is not required and the working language is English.
official.program_type: Government-funded research internship programme (DAAD / German Federal Foreign Office)
official.english_requirement: German language ability is not required unless noted in the individual project description; basic German helps in everyday life but the working language will be English.

verification.notes: Read DAAD's own RISE Germany overview, applicant-information and FAQ pages in full on 2026-10-10; the 992 Euro monthly scholarship, insurance, travel subsidies, application documents, deadlines (30 November 2026 applications, 15 December 2026 references) and the matching process are confirmed as published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an internship stipend, not a degree scholarship: 992 euros a month plus health, accident and liability insurance, an international travel subsidy and a 160-euro travel stipend for the July meeting in Heidelberg, with no tuition involved. The award is a matching system rather than an exam - providers rank applicants in January and DAAD alternates between student GPA and project demand, so a tailored motivation letter for each project and an early referee upload matter more than applying to the maximum number of offers. You must still hold undergraduate status when the internship runs, so anyone graduating before summer 2027 is excluded and belongs in RISE Professional instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Second- or third-year undergraduates in biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, earth sciences or engineering at North American, British or Irish universities who want a funded summer research internship in Germany.
application_readiness_checklist: Register for a DAAD ID early and browse offers across several fields rather than only your exact major
Write a separate motivation letter for each project, explaining how your experience prepared you for that specific position
Produce a one-page list of courses you will have completed by the internship start date
Request a transcript and a certificate of enrollment showing your expected graduation date
Ask a PhD-holding academic referee early and send them the generated upload link (deadline 15 December 2026)
Open a European (IBAN) bank account soon after arriving in Germany so stipend and travel payments can be made
common_rejection_risks: Graduating before the internship, which breaks the undergraduate status that German work-permit rules require
An incomplete application - if everything is not online by 30 November 2026, the application cannot be considered
A reference letter from a company, or from a referee without a PhD, which is not accepted
Applying to both RISE Germany and RISE Professional in the same year, which is not allowed
Restricting the project search to one field and missing relevant interdisciplinary offers
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing and daily living costs beyond the 992 euro monthly stipend; hosts assist with finding housing but DAAD publishes no housing grant, and Canadians receive their 7,000 CAD directly from Mitacs rather than DAAD.
document_audit: The transcript may be a digital version with university name, logo, student name and print date, or a copy of a certified hard copy - an 'issued to student' stamp is acceptable

The certificate of enrollment must show the university stamp, an authorized signature and the expected graduation date, because the German Federal Employment Agency needs proof of continuing student status
The reference letter must be on university letterhead, signed, and uploaded online by the referee through your generated link
alerts: The application closes 30 November 2026 at 11:59 pm CET but references run to 15 December - do not apply late and assume your referee still has time
Virtual internships exist but carry different scholarship rates, so check the project description
Stays are capped at a minimum of ten weeks and a maximum of 90 days, starting between 15 May and 15 July 2027
DAAD provides no individual feedback on unsuccessful applications, by email or phone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply entirely online in the RISE Germany internship database by 30 November 2026; your referee uploads the letter via your generated link by 15 December; providers rank candidates in January and DAAD announces positions around February/March 2027.
